title: P. Rules
description: `rules.json`: the rules the product must keep, each with the criterion its tests prove — validated by the human in the factory's design, written by the rules' task, never by a development task.

id.description: R and its number in the factory's design, never reused.

family.description: journey: a step of a user's journey, proved in a browser (tests/rules/journey); business: an invariant or a computation, proved in Rust (tests/rules/business).

criterion.description: How a test tells it is met. Each test of the rule copies the three parts as they are.

pages.description: The mock-up's pages that carry it (`pages/…`).

components.description: The micro-frontends that carry it, by name.

state.description: `conform`: the rule changed and its tests ahead of the code; a task brings the code to it. Absent: the rule stands.
